items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: they’ll start with maybe Elvin Jones or Tony Williams, which for them is going back 30 or 35 years

ctx.x: From that list it’s almost as if you went backwards in first listening to like Krupa and then listening to guys that came even before him.

Um humm, I had a starting point, which was probably the late ‘30’s and I moved on after that into the early to middle ‘40’s and then I really began getting interested in the early ‘30’s and the ‘20’s. And so I was moving in all sorts of directions. I know there are a lot on youngsters today, they’ll start with maybe Elvin Jones or Tony Williams, which for them is going back 30 or 35 years. And that’s like the beginning of the history of jazz drumming, but you just have to work back further and further. So I…

embrace, ultimately, as many of the great, great drummers, far back toward the beginning of this century and on up to somebody I might meet tomorrow afternoon or somebody that I heard play last week. And I love them all.
